goals: Understand the site's purpose, intended audience, and concrete product value.
Separate what exists today from proposed concepts and future roles.
Prepare an accurate 30-second explanation and identify questions about maturity and unsupported expectations.

viewport: Fresh isolated Chromium context, desktop 1440x1000, file URI only; supplied desktop and mobile top screenshots also inspected. No external requests were allowed. The browser's screenshot of the worksheet section and selected fee-role state were captured and viewed.

actions.action: Opened the hero disclosure labeled ‘Current maturity · scoped local evidence’.
actions.observed: It expands to a detailed maturity paragraph that calls Moriarty Webs a concept under review, describes the supplied S07 and S08 local evidence, and explicitly says there is no on-chain transaction recorded, no general Web integration, and every interactive example is an illustration.
actions.taskOutcome: Helped establish what the page says exists today and what it says remains unestablished. The disclosure is substantially denser than the hero summary.
actions.evidence: Browser observation at the hero disclosure; captured state at screenshots/maturity-open.png.

actions.action: Followed the ‘Explore’ navigation link to the Web explorer and selected the ‘Fee accounting’ proof-role row.
actions.observed: The inspector changed from ‘Payment arithmetic’ to ‘Fee accounting’. It describes the 2 CASH source fee as a separate payment and says the fee does not discharge invoice duty. The panel also says this is an illustrative requirement, with no concrete proof instance or independent producer supplied; the illustration is not verification, acceptance, or settlement.
actions.taskOutcome: Helped explain the intended product value: make financial conditions and proposed proof roles inspectable alongside a consuming transition. The role interaction is an illustration, not a usable proof integration.
actions.evidence: Actual browser selection and inspector text; screenshots/explorer.png is the supplied static reference, and screenshots/fee-role-selected.png is my captured and viewed reached state.

actions.action: Followed ‘Follow the value’ to the financial worksheet and changed the control from ‘Source behavior (S12, not executed)’ to ‘PROPOSED full-backing policy’.
actions.observed: At the displayed 35 CASH payment, the proposed policy assumes 112 CASH funding, shows 35 paid to the seller and 2 to the fee recipient, and leaves 75 cash against 75 duties. It explicitly says 112 is not an S12 action and requires a program change.
actions.taskOutcome: Helped distinguish source behavior from a proposed policy and see the page's concrete explanatory value. The interactive arithmetic should not be mistaken for Moriarty execution.
actions.evidence: Actual browser control change and visible worksheet values; screenshots/worksheet-state.png shows the reached worksheet view.

actions.action: Moved the worksheet payment slider from 35 to 50 CASH while the proposed policy was selected.
actions.observed: The page updated the seller amount to 50, the fee remained 2, cash remaining became 60, invoice duty became 50, reserve duty remained 10, and total duties became 60. It continued to label the result arithmetic rather than execution, proof verification, or settlement.
actions.taskOutcome: Helped confirm the worksheet is an interactive explanatory calculator and that its displayed policy still keeps the one-partial duties backed at the changed amount.
actions.evidence: Actual browser slider change and updated visible worksheet text in the isolated session.

questions.question: Who is the primary user expected to get value from this first: a protocol designer, a contract developer, a wallet integrator, or someone reviewing a financial application?
questions.whereItArose: The hero gives a proof-to-transition value statement, while the explorer and worksheet use developer and financial-workflow language.
questions.remainingClarification: The page names no primary audience or first adopter, so it is hard to tell whose workflow is the product's entry point.

questions.question: What can a developer actually use today, beyond this editorial prototype and its local examples?
questions.whereItArose: Hero maturity disclosure and the explorer's ‘ILLUSTRATIVE WEB’ and ‘FUTURE REQUIRED SET’ labels.
questions.answerLocation: Hero caveat says general Web integration and on-chain settlement remain unestablished and no proofs, signatures, or transactions run on this page. The expanded ‘Current maturity · scoped local evidence’ section gives the stated local evidence limits. The explorer says no concrete proof instances are supplied.
questions.remainingClarification: The page does not say whether any separately usable developer artifact or supported integration path is available now.

questions.question: Are the three explorer rows three producers or proofs that a developer could assemble, or are they proposed requirements only?
questions.whereItArose: Selecting ‘Fee accounting’ in the Web explorer.
questions.answerLocation: The explorer caption says the three rows are separate role requirements, not independent producers, existing producers, concrete Strands, proof instances, a verified set, or settlement. The inspector says no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied.
questions.remainingClarification: No further clarification needed for the scope of this illustration.

questions.question: Is 112 CASH full-backing something the current source action does, or a proposed product policy?
questions.whereItArose: Switching the worksheet from ‘Source behavior (S12, not executed)’ to ‘PROPOSED full-backing policy’.
questions.answerLocation: The worksheet says S12 has no extra-funding action, calls 112 not an S12 action, and says it requires a program change; the proposal backs one partial only.
questions.remainingClarification: No further clarification needed for this displayed example.

questions.question: Does ‘Bring the required proofs to the transition’ describe a currently available product capability or the design goal?
questions.whereItArose: The hero headline and adjacent ‘MORIARTY WEBS · PROPOSED CARDANO CONCEPT’ label.
questions.answerLocation: The adjacent hero copy calls it a proposed concept, says integration and settlement remain unestablished, and states that no proofs, signatures, or transactions run on this page.
questions.remainingClarification: The headline is aspirational, but the first-view explanation does not name a current user action with a production outcome.

findings.impact: A product lead cannot infer who should adopt the concept first or which user workflow anchors the roadmap.
findings.observation: The page presents contract and financial concepts but does not identify a primary audience. The hero promises an explicit financial-to-proof handoff, while the explorer says no concrete proof instances or producers exist.
findings.evidence: Hero audience and value copy; explorer section ‘Give every proof a defined job’ and selected-role inspector text. This is an observed omission from the inspected page, not evidence about users.
findings.suggestedChange: State the intended first audience and the concrete job this concept is meant to help them do.

findings.impact: A reader may not understand the maturity boundary or see the key distinction between a local evidence packet, a proposed concept, and a usable integration path without opening dense supporting copy.
findings.observation: The hero includes a concise caveat, but the expanded maturity disclosure contains a long paragraph with many identifiers and qualifications. The most decision-relevant facts are mixed with evidence labels and source-reading scope in one block.
findings.evidence: Visible hero disclosure state in screenshots/maturity-open.png and its expanded text: concept under review, S07/S08 evidence, no on-chain transaction, unestablished integration, and illustrative examples.
findings.suggestedChange: Keep the detailed evidence, while adding a short plain-language ‘today / proposed / not yet’ summary before the identifiers.

findings.impact: A clearer first-use cue would make the concept easier to explain to a stakeholder who has not read the page closely.
findings.observation: The hero's ‘Make the handoff from financial requirements to concrete proofs and the consuming script explicit’ is the clearest value statement, but it describes a design aim rather than a current capability.
findings.evidence: Hero paragraph and caveat immediately below the two calls to action.
findings.suggestedChange: Pair the design aim with one plain sentence saying that the current page is an interactive concept walkthrough and local arithmetic illustration.

teachBack: In my words: Moriarty Webs proposes a way for a financial application to name the proof roles a consuming transition requires and show how those roles relate to claim definitions, proof statements, context, and the consumer. A Web is described as the script-bound collection of Strands required for one transition; a Strand is an individual proof with its claim, statement, and binding metadata; a claim specification is the reusable definition of an assertion, subject, premises, and intended relation. The practical value is making assets, recipients, authority, fees, and remaining duties visible in the handoff. What exists on this page today is an editorial concept with interactive role selection and worksheet arithmetic. The page reports a limited local evidence packet, but says no on-chain transaction is recorded, no general Web integration or genuine intent authorization is established, and its interactive examples are illustrations rather than execution or settlement.
limits: This is one model persona's review, not real human user research or a population claim.
I inspected the frozen HTML only through a fresh local Chromium browser and the named screenshots; I did not inspect implementation source or other persona reviews.
I report the page's stated evidence and limits without judging cryptographic or security correctness.
I did not open external evidence links or verify claims beyond the page.
